paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon.

He was older than Rabbi Yohanan, who received teachings from him. In [Bava Batra 114b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.114b.4): “Rabbi Yohanan said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon” ([Rashbam](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Bava_Batra.114b.4.1) explains that he says “in the name of” because he was not his principal teacher); afterward: “[Rabbi Yohanan raised an objection to him](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.115a.1).” In Chullin 48b: when growths came before Rabbi Yohanan, he sent [them] to Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shimon, who permitted them in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. In [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah, beginning of chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.4.1.5), Rabbi Yohanan disagrees with him. In [Bereshit Rabbah 4:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.4.2) we find Rabbi Yudan son of Rabbi Shimon; in [5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.5.2), Rabbi Berechiah speaks in the name of Rabbi Yudan son of Shimon.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The objection follows at 115a. Hyman cites Chullin 48b. The growths and Rabbi Yehudah’s ruling in Rabbi Elazar’s name are at [Chullin 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.48a.15).

Hyman’s [printed entry](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=154) gives Bereshit Rabbah 4:2 and 5:2. The supplied Hebrew transcription reads 14:2 and 15:2. Both cited statements appear at the printed locators in the consulted text.
